description: For 50 consecutive days, tens of thousands have flooded Tirana demanding cancellation of a Kushner-backed megaresort on protected Albanian coastline — the biggest uprising since communism fell in 1991.

faqs.answer: A mass protest movement in Albania that began on May 23, 2026, opposing a multibillion-dollar luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner on protected coastline. Named for the flamingos that shelter in the Narta Lagoon that the project threatens.
faqs.question: What is the Flamingo Revolution?

faqs.answer: Five demands: non-negotiable resignation of PM Edi Rama, formation of a 12-month technical transitional government, constitutional reforms including a two-term prime minister limit, cancellation of the Sazan-Zvërnec resort project, and full repeal of Law 21/2024.
faqs.question: What are the protesters' demands?

faqs.answer: The project spans two sites: approximately $1.4 billion for Sazan Island and $4.7 billion for Zvërnec, totaling $6.1 billion. Plans include 600 townhouses, 520 villas, 1,400 apartments, a 350-superyacht marina, and a golf course across 13 million square feet.
faqs.question: How big is the Kushner resort project?

faqs.answer: An amendment to Albania's Protected Areas Law passed in 2024 that created exceptions allowing five-star tourism developments in environmentally protected areas. It was passed shortly before the resort project was announced.
faqs.question: What is Law 21/2024?

leadParagraph: Albania's Flamingo Revolution has entered its 50th day as tens of thousands protest a multibillion-dollar luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump. The movement has expanded from environmental defense into a demand for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama and an end to systemic corruption.

methodology: Reported using Foreign Policy investigation, Democracy Now! broadcast, AP, Reuters, CBS, NBC, Financial Times, BirdLife International, Guardian, DW, and Middle East Eye coverage. Protest details cross-referenced across multiple wire services. Timeline verified through Wikipedia and Albanian media.
